name: Digital Signature Assessment
description: Assessment of application-level digital signature security including signature verification correctness, algorithm confusion, signature stripping, and protocol-level misuse. Covers cross-scheme concerns (JWT, code signing, multi-signature) while algorithm-specific implementation details (RSA padding, ECDSA nonce management) are assessed under their respective algorithm skills.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to digital signature assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the purpose of digital signatures and basic signature schemes
evidence: Can explain how digital signatures provide authentication, integrity, and non-repudiation
Understands the difference between RSA-PSS and RSA-PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures
Can describe common signature algorithms (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA) and their use cases

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies signature scheme configurations and basic misuse under supervision
evidence: Identifies signature algorithms used in certificates, JWTs, and code signing
Detects use of deprecated or disallowed signature algorithms (SHA-1 based signatures; DSA, which FIPS 186-5 no longer approves for signature generation) under guidance
Reviews code for correct signature verification patterns
Documents signature-related findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses digital signature implementations for security flaws
evidence: Identifies signature stripping and algorithm confusion vulnerabilities (e.g., JWT 'none' algorithm)
Evaluates ECDSA implementations for nonce quality issues affecting signature security
Assesses signature verification for proper handling of malformed or malleated signatures
Produces findings referencing FIPS 186-5 or relevant protocol specifications

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex signature deployments; identifies subtle verification flaws
evidence: Identifies signature malleability issues in blockchain and protocol contexts
Evaluates deterministic signature schemes (RFC 6979) for correct implementation
Assesses multi-signature and threshold signature implementations
Reviews and mentors junior staff on digital signature assessment

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines signature assessment methodology; publishes research on signature security
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's digital signature assessment methodology
Published research on signature scheme vulnerabilities or novel attacks
Provides expert guidance on signature scheme selection for system design
Trains teams on signature internals, verification pitfalls, and emerging standards

assessment_methods.description: Assess a JWT-based authentication system: evaluate signature algorithm enforcement, key management, and verification correctness
Given an ECDSA-signed protocol, identify whether the implementation is vulnerable to nonce reuse and demonstrate key recovery
